full_judgment:
Quazi Reza-ul Hoque J : On an application under section 561A the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, this rule was issued calling upon the opposite- parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Complain. Case No. 7404 of2008 dated 15-12-2008 under Section 406 and 420 of the Penal Code, now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. And pending hearing of the Rule, all further proceedings of Complaint Case No. 7404 of 2008 dated 15-12-2008 under Sections 406 and 420 of the Penal Code, now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, was stayed for a period of three months and through further extensions, lastly on 7-3-2011, it was extended for another period of four (4) months. 

 2. The relevant facts for disposal of the Rule is that the complainant-opposite-party No.2, a share- holder of Export Import Bank Ltd (hereinafter referred as the Bank), filed Complaint Case No. 7404 of2008 on 15-12-2008 under Sections 406 and 420 of this Penal Code, in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka against the Chairman, Managing Director, two Directors and Company Secretary i.e. the accused-petitioner (hereinafter referred to as the accused) stating, inter alia that he was a promoter-director during the period of 2-6-1999 to 14-8-2005. And at the time of incorporation of the Bank his number of share was 100,000 @ Taka 100 per share and that number of share with bonus shares, stood at 3,25,000 on 16-11-2008. The Government through Circular No. BRPD No.8 & 12 dated 26-4-2003 directed all the commercial banks to reduce its number of Directors from 21 to 13 and also made amendment of section 15Kaka of the Banking Companies Act, 1991 to the extent that no Director shall hold office of Director for more than two (2) consecutive terms, whilst each term is for three (3) years i.e. not to hold office of Director for more than six (6) years consequently. To enter into an arrangement to constitute the future Board of Directors and for the management of the Bank on 12-8-2004, nineteen (19) Directors of the. Bank including the complainant-opposite-party No. 2 held a meeting at the Board Room of the Bank and signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) which contained as to how the future Board of the Bank will be constituted. The then Directors Md Foyez Ullah, Mrs. Nasima Akhter and Mrs. Rezwana K Reza did not sign the said MoU. 

 6. The MoU contained in its clauses 2-5, to appoint the complainant-apposite-party No. 2 and some witnesses Directors by rotation, while some of the witnesses were supposed to be Directors on rotation in the instant year (2008) but by breaching the terms of the MoU. Md Nazrul Islam, cleverly did not hold election of Directors in the Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the Bank held on 26-8-2008, referring to the case, to be decided in future and in the result complainant-apposite-party No.2, including witness Nos. 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 12 and 13 could not become Directors of the Bank in the instant year (2008), which has caused serious injury to their name & fame in the society. The accused by obtaining signatures in the MoU, of the complainant-opposite-party No. 2 and the witnesses, have benefited severally and have breached the trust of the com- plain ant-opposite-party No.2 and the witnesses and thereby caused offence under the provisions of sections 406 and 420 of the Penal Code, 1860. 

 7. "The accused-petitioner in his petition stated that due to amendment in the Section 15KaKa of the Banking Companies Act, 1991 through Section 7 of Ordinance No. XXII of 2007, position of Directors in many of the commercial banks fell squeezed and being aggrieved by the said amendment writ petition No. 6653 of 2008 has been moved challenging the constitutionally of the said amendment, wherein a Rule was issued on 26-8-2008 and an order of status quo was passed. The Complainant Case No. 7404 of 2008 under Sections 406 and 420 of the Penal Code, 1860 was filed on 15-12-2008, whilst the status quo order was already in force and the AGM of the Bank was held on 26-8-2008 wherein the election of Directors was an agenda. And due to the said order of status quo in the said writ petition, the election could not be held. 

 9. Complainant-opposite-party No.2, contested the Rule by filing a counter-affidavit contending inter alia that he had to retire from the post of Director due to amendment in 2003, of section 15 Kaka of the Banking Companies Act, 1991, which kept his door open for re-election after three years. The accused-petitioner as Company Secretary in connivance with the other accused kept the said MoU in their possession wherein there was an understanding within the Directors about the rotation of Directors. The complainant-opposite-party No.2, filed an application under section 98 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1898 (CrPC) in the concerned case but before the application could be moved the instant Criminal Miscellaneous Case was moved and an order of stay has been obtained staying all further proceedings of the concerned com. plaint case. It is also stated that accused No.1 Md Nazrul lslam through accused No.2, moved the writ petition No.6653 of 2008, along with some Directors of different banks to hang on to their positions as Directors. The order of stay in the said writ petition was passed at 12.30 pm on 26-8-2008, whereas the AGM already began at 11.00 am. The Rule that has been issued in the said writ petition was discharged on merit on 5-3-2009. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on examination of the complainant found prima facie case and there- fore took cognizance in the concerned compliant case and issued summons upon the accused. 

 10. Mr Rokonuddin Mahmud, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner has submitted that no allegation has been disclosed in the complaint-petition against the accused- petitioner that attracts sections 406 and 420 of the Penal Code. The subject matter of the concerned complaint case is concerning election of Directors, which is a matter to be dealt with in accordance with section 91 of the Companies Act, 1994 and Banking Companies Act, 1991. The election was stayed as per status quo order passed in writ petition No. 6653 of2008 on 26-08-2008 and the concerned complaint case was filed on 15-12-2008, so withholding the election in its election by the Bank on 26-8-2008, was not done at the instance of either the instant accused-petitioner, or at the instance of any other accused of the said complaint case. As the MoU has remained totally in abeyance of any use, so there is no question of anyone taking any advantage through its use. The MoU has never been disclosed. He pressed for making the Rule absolute and to quash the proceedings in the concerned complaint case. 

 11. Mr Mansurul Haque Chowdhury, the learned Senior Advocate, appearing for the complainant-opposite-party No.2, has submitted that the MoU is a tangible property, which has a value and therefore taking advantage by its use, whilst it has been kept with the accused-petitioner and other accused of the complaint case is a criminal breach of trust. He further submitted that the complainant opposite-party No.2, is a co-owner of the MoU, as such, depriving him of the right to an authenticated copy is also a criminal breach of trust and therefore the accused of the complaint case has committed offence under section 406 and 420 of the Penal Code. He also submitted that the accused Nos. 1&2, of the complaint case stands in' a fiduciary relation- ship with the other signatories of the MoU and therefore they ought to have provided an authenticated copy of the same to the complainant-opposite party No.2 and such denial attracts section 405 of the Penal Code. He also submitted that no charge sheet has been given, so the instant petition under 561A is pre-mature and therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 15. The complaint-case was filed on 15-12-2008, whilst an order of status quo was already in force passed in writ petition No. 6653 of 2008, and the election was withheld by virtue of the said status quo order dated 26-8-2008, as such the allegations made in the complaint case that the election was withheld taking advantage of the MoU is unjustified. If any anyone's right with regard to re-election for the position of Directorship as has been alleged and reiterated time and again in the complaint case is infringed, he should have sought redress under the provisions of Banking Companies Act, 1991 and the Companies Act, 1994. Any denial of right to reelection cannot be agitated through sections 406 and 420 of the Penal Code. There are specific provisions in the Companies Act, 1994 to deal with such issues. Remedies are available either through complaint to the Registrar of Joint Companies; as it is a Bank, to the Bangladesh Bank; or seeking remedy before the Company Bench of the High Court Division. In every AGM, election of Directors are supposed to held and the listed companies usually have representatives of Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to oversee the proceedings of the AGM, as such, withholding a scheduled election at the whim and caprice of a few Directors or Company Secretary is not possible as has been alleged by the complainant-opposite-party No. 2. 

 16. We do not find any usage of the said MoU and anyone taking its advantage and there is no complacency either of the accused-petitioner, or any of the accused of the complaint case as has been alleged, which nowhere at all discloses any act that could fall within the ambit of sections 406 and 420 of the Penal Code, 1860; and therefore we hold that there is no prima facie case in the Complaint Case No. 7404 and 2008, that could implicate the instant accused-petitioner; and therefore the proceedings in the said case if continued would amount to sheer abuse of process of the Court, and as such, the said proceedings is liable to be quashed. 

 17. In the result, the Rule is made absolute; and the proceedings in Complaint Case No. 7404 of 2008, under Sections 406 and 420 of the Penal Code, now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka is hereby quashed. Consequently stay order passed in this case stands vacated.
